changes.note: Third of the Leviathan subsea gathering lines; FID 2-3 Jul 2023 at US$568M (OGJ, Times of Israel); construction paused after the 7 Oct 2023 Hamas attack; completed ~3 Mar 2026 (Rigzone, citing NewMed Energy). Raises Leviathan field production capacity ~12 -> ~14 Bcm/yr (OGJ frames the same uplift as INGL export capacity 1.2 -> 1.4 Bcfd); the GEM Capacity 2 bcm/y is this line's incremental uplift. A separate, field-wide Leviathan production suspension ran ~28 Feb - early Apr 2026 on Israeli Energy Ministry orders tied to the Iran conflict (NOT pipeline-specific; production resumed Apr 2026). No length or diameter published in any source. JV: Chevron Mediterranean 39.66% (operator), NewMed Energy 45.34%, Ratio Energies 15%. Do not conflate the 2023 pipeline sanction with the Jan 2026 Phase 1B Stage 1 wells FID.

Do NOT auto-replace the route. GEM's current mid-Strip alignment is better supported than the INGL system map (which carries its own 'schematic, general-orientation only' disclaimer). The project's own Wadi Gaza EIA study (Qumsiyeh, Palestine Institute for Biodiversity) places the Gaza-side terminus/crossing at the Gaza Power Plant / Wadi Gaza corridor (mid-Strip, ~31.456N 34.401E), total route ~47 km (43 km Israel + 4 km Gaza), consistent with GEM. The INGL map's southern 'statutory planning' line near the Tzalim/Gvulot/Kerem Shalom cluster may be a different Negev line, not G4G. Any route work goes through the Route Creation SOP with the Wadi Gaza EIA as a candidate corroborating source (not GEM, not fabricated coords).

changes.to: Built by Eastern Mediterranean Gas Co (EMG); ran Egypt->Israel (El Arish->Ashkelon) May 2008-2012, then halted amid Egypt's gas shortfall/disputes. Flow reversed and restarted ~Jan 2020 (Ashkelon->El Arish), carrying Leviathan/Tamar gas to Egypt for domestic use + LNG re-export via Idku/Damietta; required physically reversing pumping stations and re-certifying the line ahead of Noble Energy's late-2019 buy-in. Briefly halted after the 9 Oct 2023 Tamar shutdown (exports rerouted via Jordan/FAJR) but recovered — 2023 Israel->Egypt exports still rose 39% y/y to a record 8.6 bcm. Ownership: 61% East Mediterranean Gas Co legacy block / 39% EMED (East Gas Company 50% + NewMed 25% + Chevron[ex-Noble] 25%). Capacity is rising 6.5 -> 8.5 bcm/y system-wide via a SEPARATE new Ashdod-Ashkelon feeder pipeline (~45-46 km, INGL, completed Jul 2026) that is NOT part of P0462 and may warrant its own Discovery look.
